reasons: Directionally correct and on-position: the redline inserts a Company (customer) convenience right on 30 days' notice with a refund of prepaid fees (preferred position) and confines HDI's (vendor/host) convenience right to end-of-term non-renewal on 90 days' notice, which satisfies both the preferred bar (no vendor mid-term walk-away) and the fallback.
Party mapping is right: in this site development/hosting agreement HDI is the host/vendor and 'the Company' (Deerskin) is our customer-side party, so the edits run in our favor.

The Termination Payment cap at three months' fees with a carve-out for HDI-fault terminations tracks the rule's express redline guidance ('replace penalties with the fallback fee cap'), and the original formula (roughly 50% of trailing annual Net Sales less $800k) is plainly a penalty far exceeding that cap.

Failed deterministic check 'Customer convenience termination present' is a phrasing artifact only — the clause uses the contract's defined party name 'the Company' rather than the literal token 'Customer'; the substantive right is present.

High changed-character ratios on p0024 and p0026 are justified: the rule requires replacing the mutual 90-day notice mechanic and neutralizing the exit penalty, and the edits otherwise preserve original structure, defined terms and the 'Termination Date' definition.
Comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural, correctly prefixed, and explains both the convenience right and the fee-cap fallback without lecturing.

Minor residual risk (not disqualifying): the carve-out cites 'Section 1.6' and the cap references fees 'pursuant to Section 3.1', neither of which is in the supplied text — confirm those cross-references before sending.
